decisions.statement: An audit judges every file this repository has.
A run narrowed to named checks says in its answer that the run is not an audit.
A named check runs even where that check runs at no audit.
An audit naming no check runs only the checks that run at audit.
A run naming no check says how many checks it left out for not yet judging.
That saying names each of those checks and the phases its own page states.
A slug naming no check is refused.
A run owed a check's verdict asks the audit service for a round over HTTP.
A run naming checks asks the audit service for those checks and no others.
A run that is the one in the cluster runs the round rather than asking for one.
A round in the cluster writes its verdicts through the pages service.
No run judges a check in the calling process.
A check a round underway answers is waited for rather than asked for again.
The round a run asks for names the commit that run needs judged.
A round underway at an older commit is opened beside rather than waited for.
No run narrows which files the checks see.
A run that asks answers for the commit the repository is at when that run opens.
A check whose verdict answers for that commit is owed no round.
A check unanswered once the asking is over is named rather than answered clean.
A run that cannot reach the audit service is refused rather than answered clean.
That refusal says what puts the audit service up rather than naming its unit.
An audit lands no change.
A refusal an audit found is kept whole beside the calling agent's page.
The answer names that file and the call opening it.
That file is the agent's audit refusals rather than the file a landing writes.
A landing after the audit leaves that file where the answer said it was.
An audit finding nothing writes nothing and names no file.
An audit whose caller has no page keeps nothing and names no file.
A phase naming no check is refused.
A check that throws refuses its own page.
An audit a check could not run in is answered as operational rather than as the data's fault.
An audit says how many checks could not run.
A refusal's reason is carried by its lines rather than as one run of words.
A reason the answer holds only part of says how much of that reason went.
An audit's findings are answered as the data's fault.
The audit service keeps running, turning a round of its own every hour.
Nothing has the folder still while an audit runs.
A change landing under an audit is judged half as that change was.
A round is asked for once.
Several seats asking at once are answered by one round.
`--check` is named again for each check asked for.

definition: the command answering every check that runs at audit, over every file this repository has
